question: In mathematics, the n! conjecture is the conjecture that the dimension of a certain bi-graded module of diagonal harmonics is n!. Resolved by Mark Haiman (2001).

question: Guralnick–Thompson conjecture. Resolved by Daniel Frohardt and Kay Magaard (2001).

title: Catalan's conjecture, 1844
question: Catalan's conjecture (or Mihăilescu's theorem) is a theorem in number theory that was conjectured by the mathematician Eugène Charles Catalan in 1842 and proven in 2002 by Preda Mihăilescu at Paderborn University. Resolved by Preda Mihăilescu (2002).

title: Poincaré conjecture, 1904
question: In the mathematical field of geometric topology, the Poincaré conjecture (UK:, US:, French: [pwɛ̃kaʁe]) is a theorem about the characterization of the 3-sphere (the hypersphere that bounds the 4-ball in four-dimensional space). Resolved by Grigori Perelman (2002).

title: Geometrization conjecture of Thurston
question: In mathematics, Thurston's geometrization conjecture (now a theorem) states that each of certain three-dimensional topological spaces has a unique geometric structure that can be associated with it. Resolved by Grigori Perelman (2003).

title: Cameron–Erdős conjecture
question: In combinatorics, the Cameron–Erdős conjecture (now a theorem) is the statement that the number of sum-free sets contained in [ N ] = { 1, …, N } is O (2 N / 2). Resolved by Ben Green; and independently by Alexander Sapozhenko (2003).

title: Nirenberg–Treves conjecture
question: Nirenberg–Treves conjecture. Resolved by Nils Dencker (2003).

title: Frobenius conjecture
question: In mathematics, specifically group theory, Frobenius's theorem states that if n divides the order of a finite group G, then the number of solutions of x n = 1 in G is a multiple of n. Resolved by Nobuo Iiyori and Hiroshi Yamaki (2004 (see comment)).

title: Stanley–Wilf conjecture
question: The Stanley–Wilf conjecture, formulated independently by Richard P. Stanley and Herbert Wilf in the late 1980s, states that the growth rate of every proper permutation class is singly exponential. Resolved by Adam Marcus and Gábor Tardos (2004).

title: Nagata's conjecture on automorphisms
question: In algebra, Nagata's conjecture states that Nagata's automorphism of the polynomial ring k[x,y,z] is wild. Resolved by Ualbai U. Umirbaev and Ivan P. Shestakov (2004).

question: Tameness conjecture. Resolved by Ian Agol; and independently by Danny Calegari–David Gabai (2004).

title: Road coloring conjecture

title: Serre's modularity conjecture
question: In mathematics, Serre's modularity conjecture, introduced by Jean-Pierre Serre (1975, 1987), states that an odd, irreducible, two-dimensional Galois representation over a finite field arises from a modular form. Resolved by Chandrashekhar Khare and Jean-Pierre Wintenberger (2008).

title: Surface subgroup conjecture
question: In mathematics, the surface subgroup conjecture of Friedhelm Waldhausen states that the fundamental group of every closed, irreducible 3-manifold with infinite fundamental group has a surface subgroup. Resolved by Jeremy Kahn and Vladimir Markovic (2009).

title: Scheinerman's conjecture
question: In mathematics, Scheinerman's conjecture, now a theorem, states that every planar graph is the intersection graph of a set of line segments in the plane. Resolved by Jeremie Chalopin and Daniel Gonçalves (2009).

title: Circular law conjecture
question: Circular law conjecture. Resolved by Terence Tao and Van H. Vu (2010).

title: Hanna Neumann conjecture
question: In the mathematical subject of group theory, the Hanna Neumann conjecture is a statement about the rank of the intersection of two finitely generated subgroups of a free group. Resolved by Joel Friedman; and independently by Igor Mineyev (2011).

title: Hsiang–Lawson's conjecture
question: In differential geometry, Lawson's conjecture states that the Clifford torus is the only minimally embedded torus in the 3-sphere S3. Resolved by Simon Brendle (2012).

title: Willmore conjecture
question: In differential geometry, the Willmore conjecture is a lower bound on the Willmore energy of a torus. Resolved by Fernando Codá Marques and André Neves (2012).

title: Bounded gap conjecture
question: Bounded gap conjecture. Resolved by Yitang Zhang (2013).

title: Kadison–Singer problem
question: In mathematics, the Kadison–Singer problem, posed in 1959, was a problem in functional analysis about whether certain extensions of certain linear functionals on certain C*-algebras were unique. Resolved by Adam Marcus, Daniel Spielman and Nikhil Srivastava (2013).

question: In mathematics, Vinogradov's mean value theorem is an estimate for the number of equal sums of powers. Resolved by Jean Bourgain, Ciprian Demeter, and Larry Guth (2015).

title: G-conjecture
question: In geometry and combinatorics, a simplicial (or combinatorial) d-sphere is a simplicial complex homeomorphic to the d-dimensional sphere. Resolved by Karim Adiprasito (2018).

title: Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture
question: The Koukoulopoulos–Maynard theorem, historically known as the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture, is a theorem in mathematics, specifically Diophantine approximation. Resolved by Dimitris Koukoulopoulos and James Maynard (2019).
